reconvene.topic: Queued tasks under the enforcing guard
reconvene.detail: SP-041's hook decides from a session pin file, and queued tasks have no session pin (PinSession is refused to them), so while spaces are applied and the guard enforces, every tool call of a queued task is refused (pin_missing). Proposed: orchd writes a task pin file keyed by ORCH_TASK_ID when it starts a run, with the space D-46 gives (the dispatching session's space; the operator's task takes its working directory's placement), which needs Dispatch to record the caller's pin. Until then, queued work stops when spaces are applied with the guard enforcing.

reconvene.topic: What SP-041 does for D-38
reconvene.detail: D-38 lets memory reads widen by a pin's space once the enforcing guard stops a session from starting a harness outside its tree. SP-041 refuses such a launch only when the command names another job's folder (cd, paths, git -C); a launch in a folder of no space, or hidden in an opaque command (bash -c "$X") under block-other-jobs (opaque_unverified), still runs, as do double forks and launchctl/open/osascript. SP-025 should not assume more, or should require strict mode or other evidence (D-39).

reconvene.topic: Accepted risk: the hook finds its files through the environment
reconvene.detail: From the SP-041 security audit (medium, accepted 2026-11-12 with reason): orch-hook locates the guard's files and orch.db through ORCH_DATA_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME and HOME, which a session can change for a harness it starts inside itself; that nested harness's hook can then read an empty or forged directory and allow every call. Accepted because the same nested harness can already drop every hook (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, --settings), so this adds no new way around the guard; the OS sandbox (SP-046) is the boundary. Proposed for SP-042: refuse tool calls that start a harness with ORCH_DATA_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME, HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or CODEX_HOME set, or a --settings override. Confirm or ask for a fix in SP-041.

reconvene.topic: Guard files need SP-042's shell-write protection
reconvene.detail: SP-041's snapshot (<data>/guard/policy.json) and pin files are protected from file tools only (the guard directory is the snapshot's one protected path). A shell write (echo, tee, cp, mv, sed -i) can still set the guard's switch to off in the snapshot or change a session's pin space, and an edit of orch.db can do the same for the fallback. SP-042 must cover <data>/guard and orch.db for shell writes, and should keep reads of the pin files allowed.

reconvene.topic: The command log stores the hook's reported decision
reconvene.detail: From the SP-041 security audit (low): orchd stores an enforced decision (refused, allowed) and its rule as the hook reports them in RecordToolEvent, without computing its own verdict or comparing guard_enforced with its own switch; any process can only write its own chain. Reserved queue room (D-37) goes only to enforced refusals of pinned sessions and tasks, so unpinned process chains cannot claim it, but a session can still fill its own reserve share with claimed refusals. Proposed: compute orchd's own would-verdict (server.guardVerdict) on the writer goroutine and flag records whose hook decision differs.

reconvene.topic: Analysis-limit refusals under load
reconvene.detail: Targets has a 100 ms budget; when the machine is loaded it can run out on an ordinary call (RC-93 (2)), and the enforcing guard then refuses it (analysis_limit). Measure how often real sessions hit analysis_limit or guard_timeout once the guard runs (orch spaces log), and raise the budget or retry if it matters. Also seen: TestTargetsAuditRound3Cost (internal/spaces) fails under -race on this Mac (a 2 MB Write took 565 ms), unrelated to SP-041's diff.

reconvene.topic: Check the enforcing guard in real sessions after release
reconvene.detail: After SP-041 ships and orchd restarts: (1) sessions started while orchd was down or an older orchd ran have no pin file; once spaces are applied with the guard enforcing, their calls are refused (pin_missing) and they must be restarted; (2) in one Claude Code and one Codex session in a configured space, try a call into another job's folder and confirm the call is refused and the reason (rule id, no path) is shown; (3) confirm 'orch spaces enforce guard off' takes effect on the next call.

reconvene.topic: Snapshot window after an apply when orchd crashes
reconvene.detail: From SP-041's independent verifier (low): ApplySpaces commits the policy, then orchd rewrites the guard snapshot. If orchd crashes between the two, the old snapshot (for example 'no policy') stays readable and the hook decides by it until orchd restarts and rewrites it at startup. Options: remove the snapshot before an apply and rewrite it after (calls during the apply then fall back to orch.db), or accept the window.

reconvene.topic: Peer identification on Linux kernels before 6.5
reconvene.detail: SP-041 identifies socket peers by SO_PEERPIDFD on Linux (D-44), which needs kernel 6.5. On older kernels (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04) no peer is identified, no session can be pinned, and once spaces are applied with the guard enforcing every tool call is refused (fails closed). Documented in docs/internals/daemon.md; orch targets macOS (D-49). Confirm, or ask for a fallback (for example SO_PEERCRED plus a start-time check) on older kernels.

reconvene.topic: SP-041 verifier lows
reconvene.detail: From the second independent verification of SP-041 (2026-11-12), all low: (1) if the hook cannot even locate its files (guardFilesFor panics: no home or data directory), the call is refused although no spaces may be configured, a narrow exception to INV-10 in favour of INV-13; (2) no test covers an unreadable pre-tool-use stdin with no spaces configured (allowed by the same path TestGuardFilesNoPolicy covers); (3) a panic recovered in decideWithin for a cwd-changed event is logged as an enforced refuse verdict (nothing is printed, the event cannot be refused), unlike the timeout branch, which marks it not enforced.

reconvene.topic: ListSessionPins is served by ListSessions
reconvene.detail: SP-050 names a ListSessionPins RPC. ListSessions (SP-016) already lists every session pin with its harness, PID, space, first directory, liveness and command-log counts, scoped per caller, so SP-050 adds no second RPC and the Spaces pane (SP-054) reads pins from ListSessions. If the pane needs a field ListSessions lacks (e.g. the chain owner of RC-81), add it to SessionInfo instead.

reconvene.topic: ScanSpaces accepted lows
reconvene.detail: From the SP-050 security audit (0 critical/high/medium). Accepted: (1) the walk lists folders through an os.Root, but each checkout is read by absolute path with handoff.CheckoutAt, which follows a linked worktree's .git pointer outside the chosen folder by design; a folder swapped for a symlink between listing and reading could make it read one .git outside the folder. Only that remote's owner/repo reaches the operator. (2) The one-scan-at-a-time slot is a package variable, shared by every server in the process (one per orchd). (3) gh profile checks have no single-flight: a scan and a Status call at the same moment can each start a gh auth check for the same profile. (4) A placement or gh error is returned to the operator verbatim (no terms or tokens).

reconvene.topic: Space of client notes from the operator, queued tasks and unidentified callers
reconvene.detail: SP-023 places a client Ingest only in the caller's pinned space; the operator at a terminal ('orch ingest'), queued tasks and unidentified callers have none, so under a policy their notes go to quarantine until retagged (SP-071). D-46 says a task writes to its dispatcher's space, but tasks do not record the dispatching session yet (SP-025.1.a8/SP-029). Decide how the operator's own notes are placed (e.g. an operator-only space choice, or the placement of the operator's cwd).

reconvene.topic: Registered web sources outside any bound prefix go to quarantine
reconvene.detail: The sources registry does not record who registered a source, so a web source is placed by its bound web prefix only and otherwise quarantined (D-14 places a page by the session that ingested it, which a scheduled refresh does not have). Decide whether SaveSource records the registering caller's space, or the operator binds prefixes.

reconvene.topic: Local files placed only by a checkout's remote are quarantined
reconvene.detail: Security review of SP-023: an agent can make a .git naming any org, so an edit hand-off placed by its remote alone or by a remote stricter than its root, and a repo/owner source under no root, go to quarantine. A genuine org checkout under a personal or public root therefore has its edit hand-offs quarantined until hand-offs carry the editing session's space (SP-029). Registered sources under a root still follow the stricter remote, as session pins do (SP-022). Also consider making SaveSource/RefreshSource for repo/owner kinds operator-only, or limiting repo sources to sources.known_roots.

reconvene.topic: SP-023 security review lows and accepted limits
reconvene.detail: From three security-audit rounds on PR #173 (all critical/high/medium fixed): (1) a session's records are tied to it only when the transcript sits where its harness keeps that session's transcript, so planting another session's content now takes a write into ~/.claude/projects or ~/.codex/sessions (or a symlinked root there), which the OS sandbox should deny (SP-046); recording the transcript path at the pin (PinSession, orchd.proto) would close it fully; a harness whose transcripts live elsewhere (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CODEX_HOME set for the harness but not for orchd) has its session records quarantined under a policy; (2) the owner's GitHub node ID is recorded in each docs chunk's origin but not compared with the binding at placement, because the REST node_id read at apply and the GraphQL id read at sync may use different ID formats (verify, then compare in Engine.PlaceUnder); (3) the Ingest refusal to replace another space's source is an existence oracle, as the docs-kept refusal already is, and has a small check-then-write window; notes in quarantine can be replaced by any other unplaced caller; (4) DeleteSource still deletes a source in any space (gate deletes by space in SP-025/SP-026); (5) when reading the stored copy fails (Qdrant briefly unavailable), Ingest skips both replace checks, as the docs-kept check already did; (6) a .git an agent writes under a root can still move a source it registers into a stricter space (never public), accepted as for session pins.

reconvene.topic: Content stored before SP-023 has no placement
reconvene.detail: Chunks written before SP-023 carry no origin, space or labels_v, and a migration copies them as they are. A docs file whose content and repo HEAD did not change, and a source file whose text did not change, is not written again, so it keeps no placement (or an earlier one) until 'orch rag relabel' (SP-027); a repo whose visibility flips without a new HEAD is not re-stamped (SP-030.1.a2). Repo visibility and owner node ID are recorded on chunks only, not in docs_repos (no migration added, to keep parallel lanes rebase-friendly). Readers must treat a missing space or stale labels_v as unreadable (INV-08, SP-025/SP-027).

reconvene.topic: Keep the live guard's records replayable (SP-041)
reconvene.detail: Replay (SP-047) reads a recorded verdict from a command log record with spaces.RecordedVerdict: 'would <verdict> (<rule>)' in the rule for a call not enforced (daemon wouldRule), or decision 'refused' / 'allowed' with the bare rule id for one enforced; a record with decision 'logged' and no rule counts as having no recorded verdict. It rebuilds the guard event with spaces.GuardEventOf (stored targets JSON; a cwd-changed event runs in old_cwd and moves to new_cwd) and builds the guard policy with no protected paths. SP-041 (and SP-042's protected paths) should record in one of those forms, build its event with GuardEventOf, and share the protected-path list with replay; otherwise replay reports changes no policy made. The record also does not keep the guard mode it was judged in, so replay judges in the current switch or --mode; consider storing the mode with each decision.

reconvene.topic: Two open PRs extend orchd.proto
reconvene.detail: SP-050 (https://github.com/willesq/orchestrator/pull/170: ListSpaces, ScanSpaces) and SP-047 (https://github.com/willesq/orchestrator/pull/174: ReplaySpaces) were both branched from origin/main and both add RPCs and messages to orchd.proto, so the generated Go and Swift stubs will conflict when the second merges. Resolve by merging the .proto (both sides are additive) and running make proto, never by editing generated files; also keep both sides' test-fake stubs (internal/{cli,hook,mcpserver} fakeClient) and both callers.go operatorActions entries.

reconvene.topic: Replay validation runs without a deadline (accepted low)
reconvene.detail: From the SP-047 security audit (0 critical/high; the one medium was fixed). ReplaySpaces validates the revision or policy it replays under (InGitTree checks and symlink resolution of up to 512 roots, terms and gh_config_dir paths) with no deadline. A draft an agent session saved can be named by --policy <rev>, so a root on an automount or network path could stall that RPC or make the Mac contact a host. Only the operator can call it, and diff and apply validate drafts the same way. Option: validate under the request deadline in a goroutine abandoned on cancellation, and say in the reply when the named revision is an agent's unapplied draft.

reconvene.topic: Replay of session logs runs in orchd (new ReplaySpaces RPC)
reconvene.detail: The session form of 'orch spaces replay' asks orchd (ReplaySpaces, operator-only) rather than reading orch.db and the command log from the CLI: stored revisions name every job's orgs and roots (DiffSpaces is operator-only for that reason) and the log is readable only by the operator or its own session (INV-12), so reading them client-side would bypass those gates. The payload-file form stays in the CLI with no orchd, so CI can replay the SP-001 fixtures. An argument holding '/' or '.' is a path (log owners cannot hold either). Payload fixtures carry no recorded verdicts, so CI compares their replayed verdicts with a committed golden file.

reconvene.topic: GitHub calls the live guard can only mark opaque
reconvene.detail: SP-043 marks these opaque, so block-other-jobs allows them (opaque_unverified) and only strict refuses: a git remote behind an ssh alias whose host name does not say GitHub (the usual per-account setup, e.g. Host work-gh), a checkout config with url.*.insteadOf or an include (the user's global git config is not read at all), gh api graphql, gh aliases and extensions, and gh search beyond the accounts it names. Proposed: read the ssh client config's Host/HostName for aliases and the global git config's insteadOf, or refuse opaque remote-talking git and gh calls in block-other-jobs. GIT_DIR set as a shell variable is not followed either.

reconvene.topic: SP-043 verifier lows
reconvene.detail: From the independent verification of SP-043 (2026-11-12), all low: (1) a GitHub search through curl with org: in the URL query (api.github.com/search/code?q=org:X) is not read and not opaque, so it is allowed even in strict; (2) in strict, gh repo list and gh search for the session own org, and git push to a non-GitHub remote, are refused as opaque_strict; (3) for a named remote, pushurl is judged on fetch as well as url (over-inclusive, not a bypass). See also RC-114.

reconvene.topic: Wire SP-042's protection into the guard at rebase
reconvene.detail: SP-042 adds spaces.ProtectedPaths and NewGuardPolicyProtecting, but on main nothing builds a guard policy yet (the enforcing hook is SP-041, PR #172). When the two meet, orchd's guard snapshot must carry ProtectedPaths(home, config dir, data dir, applied policy) (its Write, Anywhere and Read lists, replacing SP-041's single protected guard directory) and the hook must build its policy with NewGuardPolicyProtecting; replay (SP-047) should use the same function.
reconvene.note: Resolved 2026-11-12 in commit f88994eb7c2d5f95de2bf9ba6b1ba83ea0055b9c (PR #175): orchd's guard snapshot (version 2) carries spaces.GuardProtection (ProtectedPaths for the applied policy, the guard directory and orch's binaries), orch-hook builds its policy with NewGuardPolicyProtecting from it, and orchd's ReplaySpaces and the CLI's payload replay compute the same protection. Verified by an independent verifier at 7ffc5bb (TestGuardSelfProtectionLive, TestReplaySpacesReproducesSelfProtection, TestSpacesReplayFixturesSelfProtection). Security-review lows: RC-200..RC-205.

reconvene.topic: Self-protection gaps left after the SP-042 review
reconvene.detail: Accepted for now (best-effort target extraction, D-28; the OS sandbox is the boundary): recursive reads of a directory holding secret files (grep -r or rg over the ssh or gh profile directories, tar of them) are allowed; 'git config core.hooksPath|core.fsmonitor|core.sshCommand' is not refused (writing .git/config directly is); writes by interpreters (perl -pi, python open()) and copies that create protected files without naming them (cp -r template/.claude .) are not caught. Proposed: refuse recursive readers of those directories and those git config keys.

reconvene.topic: Which secret files the guard refuses to read
reconvene.detail: SP-042 refuses reads (not only writes) of terms files and of the secret files listed in docs/internals/hooks.md (Self-protection): the files of each space's gh profile and of the default gh profile, orch's Qdrant API key, the netrc file, the AWS CLI's key file and ssh private keys (id_*, not *.pub). Confirm the list or extend it (for example Docker, kubectl, npm or PyPI login files).

reconvene.topic: TestToolHookCost flake on Linux CI
reconvene.detail: On PR #175 (no daemon change) CI failed once in TestToolHookCost (internal/daemon): one of 1,000 events reached orchd attributed to no session instead of sess-hook; a re-run passed. It also passes 5/5 locally. Likely a load-dependent race in caller resolution of the real orch-hook process on shared runners; worth a look before the enforcing guard relies on pins (a hook resolved to no session is refused while enforcing). Also from the SP-042 verifier (low): perl -i and xargs touch writes are opaque, allowed in block-other-jobs and refused in strict (see RC-111).

reconvene.topic: Self-protection follows orchd's directories, not the hook's or the harness's
reconvene.detail: From the RC-110 security review (low, accepted 2026-11-12): orchd computes the guard's protection from its own environment, and under launchd or brew services it has no ORCH_*/XDG_* variables, so it protects ~/.config/orch, ~/.claude/settings* and ~/.codex/*. A config directory or harness home that only the user's shell moves (XDG_CONFIG_HOME, ORCH_CONFIG_DIR, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME) is not protected, so an agent could edit the installed AGENTS.md or the live harness settings there. Related to RC-102. Proposed: the hook adds its own paths.ConfigDir(), data directory and guard directory to the snapshot's write list (a union only adds protection), and protects $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings* and $CODEX_HOME/{hooks.json,config.toml} when set; replay would then need the same union.

reconvene.topic: Guard snapshot version 2 refuses calls until orchd restarts after brew upgrade
reconvene.detail: From the RC-110 security review (low, fail closed): RC-110 bumped the guard snapshot to version 2. brew upgrade relinks orch-hook at once but does not restart orchd (the formula's caveat), so with a spaces policy applied and the guard enforcing, every tool call is refused as policy_unreadable until 'brew services restart orch'. Installs with no policy ever applied are allowed (the hook treats another version like a missing snapshot then). Documented in docs/internals/hooks.md. Proposed: name the version mismatch and the restart in the refusal reason, or restart orchd from the formula's post_install.

reconvene.topic: Only the orch binaries beside orchd are protected
reconvene.detail: From the RC-110 security review (low): spaces.GuardProtection protects orch, orchd and orch-hook in the directory orchd runs from (under brew services /opt/homebrew/opt/orch/bin, whose links resolve to the same Cellar files as the bin/orch-hook link harness settings run, so writes through either are refused). An orch-hook installed elsewhere (orch install --bin-dir) is not protected, and moving the whole directory that holds the settings' link (mv /opt/homebrew/bin ...) and planting a new orch-hook is not refused. Proposed: protect the hook command path orch install writes into harness settings (recorded at install, or read from the settings when the snapshot is written).

reconvene.topic: The CLI's payload replay protects its own environment's paths
reconvene.detail: From the RC-110 security review (low, replay correctness only): orch spaces replay <payloads> --policy <file> builds its protection with spaces.GuardProtection from the CLI's own ORCH_CONFIG_DIR/ORCH_DATA_DIR/HOME and its executable's directory, which can differ from the running orchd's (brew bin vs opt path, --bin-dir, a shell that sets XDG_*). orchd's ReplaySpaces uses orchd's own, the same as the live snapshot. Proposed: document, or have the CLI ask orchd for the protection it applies.

reconvene.topic: A relative orch directory or no home makes the guard refuse every call
reconvene.detail: From the RC-110 security review (low, fail closed): orchd puts ORCH_CONFIG_DIR/ORCH_DATA_DIR as written, and the home from os.UserHomeDir, into the snapshot's protection. If one is relative, or the home cannot be found, NewGuardPolicyProtecting rejects the entries and the hook answers every call with policy_unreadable while a policy is configured (with no policy nothing is refused: protection is ignored then). Nothing in orchd's log or orch status explains it. Proposed: orchd makes the directories absolute, or validates the protection before writing the snapshot and reports the failure.

reconvene.topic: Self-protection scope notes from the RC-110 review
reconvene.detail: Info-level notes from the three RC-110 security-review rounds: (1) user hook scripts that harness settings point at (~/.claude/hooks/*), shell startup files (~/.zshenv, ~/.zshrc, ~/.bash_profile), Gemini and Codex extension directories and the Homebrew tap formula run code in later sessions and are plain, recognisable writes, but are not protected; (2) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*orch* also protects unrelated launch agents whose name holds 'orch' (com.pytorch...), and writing the LaunchAgents directory itself is refused; narrow to com.orchestrator.* and homebrew.mxcl.orch*.plist if that matters; (3) the '.pub' exclusion meant for ~/.ssh/id_* also applies to write patterns (com.orchestrator.orchd.plist.pub is writable, harmless); (4) a replay judges older revisions with today's protection, so events recorded before RC-110 can show as changed where they wrote a path protected since (documented in daemon.md).

reconvene.topic: SP-072 manual checks: switch each layer from the app; review the snapshots
reconvene.detail: SP-072.1.a1 and a2 are manual. a1: with this branch's app opened by the user (not from an agent session, since SetEnforcement is operator-only), switch each of memory, guard, terms and sandbox from Settings -> Spaces (and the menu bar panel), confirm each change shows in `orch status` within 2 s, and set one for 15 minutes to see its countdown; then switch them back. a2: review the four snapshots listed in SP-072.1's evidence (section and banner, light and dark).
reconvene.note: 2026-11-12: PR #169 merged before these checks (D-57). The user's first attempt showed 'unknown method GetEnforcement' because the running Homebrew orchd (started 2026-11-09) predates SP-070; the switch check needs an orchd built from main or a separate test orchd.

reconvene.topic: The app mirrors orchd's 'relaxed' rule to decide what to confirm
reconvene.detail: EnforcementSwitch.relaxes(to:) in macos/Sources/OrchKit/Spaces.swift treats 'off' (every layer) and the guard's 'log' as relaxing, matching internal/spaces Layer.Relaxed today. If orchd adds a relaxing state, the app would switch to it without asking. A per-state relaxed flag in EnforcementSwitch (orchd.proto; lane C owns proto) would remove the copy. Also a step down that still enforces (guard strict -> block-other-jobs) is sent without confirmation, by the same definition (security audit, informational).

reconvene.topic: Low/accepted security notes from SP-072's audit
reconvene.detail: Accepted: (1) an agent with Accessibility or UI-scripting permission could click the app's switch and its confirmation, bypassing the process-ancestry check, as it could by scripting Terminal to run `orch spaces enforce`; the app adds no new class of bypass, and the log and start digest still announce it. (2) With both the Settings window and the menu bar panel open, a relaxing switch can show its confirmation in both; dismissing either cancels, which fails safe. Fixed before commit: orchd strings in the confirmation prompt, menus, banner and kinds now go through displaySafe; a folder picked in the open panel is checked untrimmed.

reconvene.topic: App snapshot mode is an offscreen test target
reconvene.detail: The app had no snapshot mode, so SP-072 adds the OrchAppSnapshots test target (Package.swift), which @testable-imports OrchApp and draws views offscreen with cacheDisplay when ORCH_SNAPSHOT_DIR is set; it is skipped otherwise, so CI writes nothing. Offscreen drawing does not show window chrome, focus or vibrancy exactly as on screen. Unverified assumption: GitHub's macos-26 runner keeps building the extra test target (it compiles but is skipped) within the app job's time. The user may want a fuller snapshot mode (every pane) later.

reconvene.topic: SP-072 adds a Go test that keeps the app's placement fixture honest
reconvene.detail: The lane rule was 'no Go daemon code'. SP-072 adds only internal/daemon/placement_app_fixture_test.go (test code): it compares macos/Tests/Fixtures/placement-explanations.json with ExplainPlacement's live answers for the plan's nested-root fixture and rewrites it with ORCH_UPDATE_APP_FIXTURE=1. A change to placement rules or explanation text therefore needs the fixture regenerated in the same PR.

reconvene.topic: Combine the outbound terms check with the enforcing guard at rebase
reconvene.detail: SP-044 runs its check in orch-hook pre-tool-use on its own (branched from main before SP-041, PR #172, merged): it prints its own deny and the command log does not record the refusal as a decision. When the two meet: one deny path, the terms refusal recorded in the command log as refused with rule outbound_term or outbound_unchecked, the hook tests' TestMain (SP-041) covering the terms tests, and the terms check reading the terms layer switch from SP-041's snapshot instead of orch.db. SP-042's ProtectedPaths already refuses reads of terms files.
reconvene.note: 2026-11-14: resolved in PR #177 (merge commit c6bccb1, verified at 190d97191df42f39b8706ff883225a12e39e2b1d): one deny path (writeDeny), terms refusals recorded through RecordToolEvent as enforced refusals with rule outbound_term or outbound_unchecked, the hook's terms tests under SP-041's TestMain, the terms layer switch read from the guard snapshot (GuardSnapshot.Terms), and replay carrying recorded terms verdicts (GuardEnforcement.Terms).

reconvene.topic: What the outbound terms check does not see
reconvene.detail: Accepted for now and documented (docs/internals/hooks.md, Outbound terms): text sent by a script or program that runs git itself (./deploy.sh, make), an interpreter, curl to the GitHub API, or a tool other than a shell (notably GitHub MCP tools), and commits a push would send that a session hid by moving local remote-tracking refs. gh search and gh api GET queries send terms to GitHub without publishing them. Proposed: cover GitHub MCP tools' write calls the same way, and compare with git ls-remote before a push when a remote's tracking ref moved in the same session.
reconvene.note: 2026-11-14: settled by D-60 (best-effort, loosened baseline in SP-044; configurable rules in SP-075).

reconvene.topic: How strict the outbound terms check is
reconvene.detail: While the terms layer is on, SP-044 fails closed (outbound_unchecked) on any outbound command it cannot read in full: a variable or command substitution in it (except $HOME and $(cat <<'EOF' ...)), a command name built from a variable, loops, eval/xargs, git -c beyond a small allowlist, an earlier command that changes a remote or config, gh fed from a pipe. A gh write without -R counts every remote of the checkout (and GH_REPO) as a destination, so a fork whose upstream is another space's refuses the session's own terms in gh pr create. After git add/commit in the same call a push also checks the work tree, untracked files and every branch. Confirm this strictness, or say which cases should be allowed.
reconvene.note: 2026-11-14: settled by D-60 (best-effort, loosened baseline in SP-044; configurable rules in SP-075).

reconvene.topic: Outbound terms elsewhere than the command log (INV-07)
reconvene.detail: SP-044 keeps terms out of refusals, the command log, orchd's log and status output. Session transcripts, session records and anything indexed into RAG from them, the PR digests and event streams can still hold a term a session typed; INV-07 lists SP-053 for those. The terms cache in orchd notices a changed terms file by size and modification time only.

reconvene.topic: Programs that run git themselves (accepted risk, D-60)
reconvene.detail: Accepted under D-60 and RC-117, recorded by the SP-044 security reviews of 2026-11-14: gh pushing an unpushed head branch itself (its interactive prompt), external git-<name> subcommands on PATH (git town, git-spr) that an alias check finds no alias for, gh's interactive base-repo prompt for a fork under a PTY (Codex exec_command with a tty), and gh api --hostname or -R naming another host. The check does not read what these send; SP-045's git hooks and per-job accounts are the boundary.

reconvene.topic: Encoded content in outbound text (accepted risk, D-60)
reconvene.detail: Accepted under D-60: the outbound terms check matches text as written. A term inside compressed, base64, UTF-16 or otherwise encoded content, a binary file over 1 MiB or past the 64th binary file of one check, or a binary file only a merge commit adds is not found.

reconvene.topic: Non-github.com hosts in gh repo names
reconvene.detail: Low (SP-044 review round 1): parseRepo drops the host, so gh -R ghe.example.com/acme/x or a PR URL on an Enterprise host is placed by the github.com owner acme, while GH_REPO with a host gives no space. Proposed: treat a repo on another host than github.com as holding no space.

reconvene.topic: A terms refusal hides the logging guard's own verdict
reconvene.detail: Low (SP-044 review round 1): with the guard off or logging, a call the terms check refuses is recorded as refused with the terms rule, so the command log loses the would-verdict the guard gave the same call (RC-86). Proposed: record both, e.g. the guard's would-rule in a second field.

reconvene.topic: Replay of terms verdicts and redacted fields
reconvene.detail: Low (SP-044 review round 1, RC-116): replay cannot run the terms check again (the log never keeps the text, INV-07, and the checkout moves on), so it carries a recorded outbound_term or outbound_unchecked refusal while the replayed guard lets the call through and the terms layer is on. Replay and orchd's logging-mode verdicts are also computed on redacted directories and targets, so a root or repo whose name is a term can replay differently from the live verdict.

reconvene.topic: Outbound calls refused when the guard cannot decide
reconvene.detail: Low, fail-closed (SP-044 review round 1): when the guard's decision times out, or its snapshot cannot be read while the guard is off or logging, the terms check cannot know the terms or the layer's switch from the snapshot and refuses every outbound call (outbound_unchecked), even when no space has terms. While the snapshot is unreadable the switch is read from orch.db, so an operator who switched terms off is not refused.

reconvene.topic: Multi-word literal terms are whitespace-exact
reconvene.detail: Low (SP-044 review round 1): a literal term of two words matches only with the single space written; two spaces, a tab or a newline between the words is not found. Proposed: match any run of blanks between a literal term's words.

reconvene.topic: Command log keeps terms split by shell quoting
reconvene.detail: Low, INV-07 (SP-044 review round 2): the command log redacts the tool input's decoded JSON text, not the words as the shell passes them, so gh issue create -b fal''con is stored as written. The check itself reads the shell words. Proposed: redact, or withhold the command, when a shell-decoded word holds a term.

reconvene.topic: Which remote gh picks, unverified cases
reconvene.detail: Low (SP-044 review rounds 1-2): gh only counts remotes on hosts it is signed in to. When gh is signed in to an Enterprise host only, it skips github.com remotes and may pick a later one; the check assumes github.com is known. The check counts gh api's {owner}/{repo} as the marked repo plus the first remotes, since gh api may ignore gh repo set-default (not checked against gh's source). Whether GitHub resolves dot segments in API paths is unverified; such paths fail closed.

Steps: (1) optional for a5's gh part: mkdir -p <dir> && GH_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> gh auth login (a job or test account). reconvene.topic: Which folders the generated rules deny
reconvene.detail: Rules deny only other isolated spaces' roots (plus other spaces' orch folders and gh profiles), never public roots or private spaces, matching block-other-jobs (D-12). A job session can therefore read a private space it does not list (e.g. personal) through the shell. Options: keep; or also deny private roots an isolated space does not read.

reconvene.topic: Cross-space channels the deny rules leave open
reconvene.detail: Not denied: harness transcripts under ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions (shared by sessions started without the launcher), orch's data folder outside spaces/ (orch.db, toollog.db; SP-042), the default gh login ~/.config/gh, the shared /tmp (D-53 residual) and /tmp/claude, which checkouts with no space share (no per-checkout TMPDIR).

reconvene.topic: What the rules reveal and how exactly they match
reconvene.detail: Each checkout's settings name other jobs' root paths (sessions can read which folders are denied; name roots neutrally). Claude Code permission rules match by case while APFS usually is not case sensitive; paths holding glob characters get only the sandbox deny.

reconvene.topic: Unverified Claude Code behaviour SP-046 relies on
reconvene.detail: Read from the Claude Code 2.1.309 binary, not measured: sandboxed commands get TMPDIR=$CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR (set through settings env), and the sandbox already denies shell writes to .claude/settings*.json. Not known: whether sandbox.filesystem.allowRead in a subfolder's own .claude (which applies to sessions started there, SP-004) or in a project settings.json can re-allow a denied folder; such subfolder files are not managed. RC-180's run checks the first.
reconvene.note: 2026-11-12, measured with Claude Code 2.1.309 headless haiku sessions: the first part was wrong. A settings file's env CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR or TMPDIR (settings.local.json, also with a 12-byte path) does not change the sandboxed TMPDIR, which stayed /tmp/claude-<uid>, nor the CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR the shell sees (also /tmp/claude-<uid>); other env entries (GH_CONFIG_DIR, an arbitrary name) do reach the shell. CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR in the process environment does: TMPDIR=<it>/claude-<uid>, but only when that path is at most 44 bytes; a 66-byte one fell back to /tmp/claude-<uid> (the binary names the AF_UNIX socket limit). No sandbox setting names a temp folder. SP-046 now keeps temp folders under /tmp/orch-<uid> and sets them through 'orch run' (RC-206 for sessions started without it). The second part held in the 'protect' probe (shell writes to .claude refused). Still not known: whether a subfolder's own .claude settings can re-allow a denied folder. 2026-11-14: RC-208 depends on the remaining question in a related form: whether sandbox.filesystem.allowRead can re-allow a folder that a permissions.deny Read rule (orch's installed Read(~/.config/gh/**)) denies to sandboxed commands. Not measured. 2026-11-14, measured with Claude Code 2.1.309: sandbox.filesystem.allowRead in a checkout's settings.local.json re-opens a folder that a permissions.deny Read rule (the installed Read(~/.config/gh/**)) denies to sandboxed commands; an allowRead in the checkout's own .claude/settings.json, or beside the deny in settings.local.json, re-opens a sandbox.filesystem.denyRead there too (RC-215); a denyRead given through --settings was not re-opened by a project settings.json allowRead. Resolved: the open question is answered.

reconvene.topic: Checkout placement spends GitHub lookups
reconvene.detail: Each sync places every checkout through orchd's repo lookups (30 per minute, cached 10 minutes), shared with session pins. With many checkouts some fall back to the remote's owner with unknown visibility until cached; rules can flip between a space's and a checkout with no space's. Consider cache-only lookups or a longer TTL for the sync.

reconvene.topic: Show checkout-settings problems outside orchd's log
reconvene.detail: Tracked files (no rules), entries moved aside, unmergeable files replaced and a truncated walk are logged by orchd only. Surface them in orch status and the app (SP-072), and recheck ignore status periodically (a checkout seen ignored is not checked again until orch changes its file).

reconvene.topic: A checkout only its remote places gets no space's rules
reconvene.detail: After the security audit (H-1), a checkout gets a space's rules only when its folder root decided the placement; a job repo cloned under a personal root gets a checkout-with-no-space's rules (no GH_CONFIG_DIR, no TMPDIR). Options: keep (move such clones under the job's root); or let the operator pin a checkout to a space.

reconvene.topic: Which folders 'orch run' accepts
reconvene.detail: Interpretation of SP-046.2.a1 'a space the current folder resolves outside of': refused when the folder is placed in another space or its placement is a conflict or quarantine; allowed in the space's own folders and in folders no root or remote places (e.g. ~/scratch). --force allows any.

reconvene.topic: Sandboxed git cannot change tracked .claude files
reconvene.detail: Each checkout's rules deny shell writes to its .claude folder, so a git checkout or pull run by the session that changes tracked files under .claude/ fails; the file tools and the user's terminal are unaffected.

reconvene.topic: SP-046 security audit lows (four rounds)
reconvene.detail: Accepted: (1) the session controls .git, so it can point the info/exclude orch appends its one ignore line to at another repository's git folder, and appendLine follows links in folders above the git folder; (2) moved-aside names (*.orch-moved-*) are not git-ignored and moving does not re-check the entry just before the rename; (3) a .claude or settings file that cannot be opened (mode 000, a socket) is reported but not moved, leaving that checkout without rules; (4) a tracked settings file gets no rules and a session can freeze its rules with git add -f (the enforcing guard, SP-041, is the answer); (5) the launcher's profile links share plugins and skills across spaces; (6) GetEnforcement is open to every caller (pre-existing).

reconvene.topic: Confirm a per-space Claude Code login persists
reconvene.detail: SP-004 measured that a fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR starts logged out but not whether its login persists. After the first 'orch run <space> -- claude' and /login, start it again and note whether it asks to log in.
reconvene.note: 2026-11-14: D-59 makes per-space logins optional; the e2e checks run with the default gh login and Claude config. 2026-11-14: now applies only to a space that names its own claude_config_dir (D-59); the per-space profile orch generated under <data dir>/spaces/<space>/claude is gone, 'orch run' uses the user's own config otherwise. Not exercised in the 2026-11-14 run.

reconvene.topic: Claude Code sessions started in a checkout share one TMPDIR across spaces (SP-046.1.a6)
reconvene.detail: Measured 2026-11-12 with Claude Code 2.1.309 (RC-184 note): only CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR in the environment Claude Code starts with sets its sandboxed commands' TMPDIR; a settings file cannot, and no sandbox setting can. So a session started in a checkout without 'orch run' writes its temp files to /tmp/claude-<uid>, which every such session of every space can read; the per-checkout settings cannot give a space its own TMPDIR, and SP-046.1.a6 is not met on that path. Denying /tmp/claude-<uid> in the checkout settings breaks temp files (mktemp 'Operation not permitted'). What holds: 'orch run' sessions get their space's TMPDIR (/tmp/orch-<uid>/<space>/claude-<uid>), are denied /tmp/claude-<uid>, and every space's settings deny every other space's temp folder, so a file a launched session writes there is unreadable from other spaces however they start. Options: (a) require 'orch run' for Claude Code sessions in isolated spaces and treat a6's per-checkout half as the launcher's (needs a criteria change by the user); (b) deny /tmp/claude-<uid> in isolated spaces' checkout settings and accept broken temp files there; (c) accept the shared folder as a documented limit until Claude Code honours a settings value (ask upstream); (d) have orch start sessions some other way that sets the environment (shell alias or wrapper the user installs).
reconvene.note: Resolved 2026-11-14 as D-58 (option c).

reconvene.topic: Security audit lows on the /tmp temp folders (SP-046)
reconvene.detail: From the 2026-11-12 audit of the temp-folder move (its medium, settings naming a temp folder orch could not make its own, was fixed: such a space gets no TMPDIR, TestSyncFailsClosedOnTmpRoot). Lows left: (1) a temp folder of a deleted or renamed space stays under /tmp/orch-<uid> and is no longer denied, and the root itself is not denied, so any session can list the space names in it; remove or deny entries that belong to no current space. (2) hashed folder names use 48 bits and a collision between two long names is not detected (both spaces would share and deny one folder). (3) EnsurePrivateDir makes an existing root of orch's own owner-only after the fact; entries others made while it was open are not checked. (4) After a reboot clears /tmp, another local user can make /tmp/orch-<uid> before orchd's first sync; orchd then refuses it and reports it, and sessions get no TMPDIR until the user removes it. Re-audit lows: (5) a /tmp/orch-<uid> root another user planted as a link, with space-named entries linking elsewhere, makes the real-path step add those targets to every space's denies (extra denies only, so sessions can break, nothing is exposed); skip denying a space's temp folder by its real path when the root failed its check. (6) Likewise a planted /tmp/claude-<uid> link adds its target to the launcher profile's denies.

reconvene.topic: gh in sandboxed agent shells with the default login (SP-046.1.a5)
reconvene.detail: Measured 2026-11-14 (Claude Code 2.1.309, TestClaudeE2E gh and launcher/gh): with the sandbox on, 'gh auth status' in a sandboxed shell fails with 'open ~/.config/gh/config.yml: operation not permitted', in checkout and launched sessions alike. orch's per-space rules do not deny ~/.config/gh; the Read(~/.config/gh/**) credential deny that 'orch install' adds to ~/.claude/settings.json does, since Claude Code applies Read deny rules to sandboxed commands too (SP-004). So under D-59 gh does not work at all in an agent shell of a space without its own gh profile. Options: (a) orch's checkout and launcher settings add the default gh folder ($GH_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.config/gh) to sandbox.filesystem.allowRead for spaces naming no gh profile (unmeasured whether allowRead overrides a permission-rule deny, RC-184; whether gh then reaches the keychain and api.github.com from the sandbox is also unmeasured; sandboxed commands could then read hosts.yml, which with keyring storage names the user but holds no token); (b) sandbox.excludedCommands ['gh'] so gh runs outside the sandbox (gh could then read or upload other jobs' files, weakening the deny); (c) narrow or drop orch's installed Read(~/.config/gh/**) deny (cc-safety-net still guards shell commands that name the files); (d) amend SP-046.1.a5 so the gh part applies only to a space with its own gh profile, documenting that gh does not work in sandboxed shells with the default login.
reconvene.note: Resolved 2026-11-14 as D-61 (option a, plus the sandbox setting auto|on|off). 2026-11-14: implemented as D-61 decided: allowRead of the default gh folder for a space on the default login, its own profile for one naming it; measured that gh also needs sandbox.network.allowedDomains (api.github.com, github.com) and sandbox.enableWeakerNetworkIsolation (Go TLS through trustd), which orch writes too (RC-213). TestClaudeE2E gh and launcher/gh PASS at 6baf911.

reconvene.topic: D-59 and orchd's GitHub routing for isolated spaces without a gh profile
reconvene.detail: D-59 says orch uses whichever gh login is already authenticated for every space. orchd's gh routing from SP-063 (internal/daemon/ghprofiles.go, docs/internals/config.md 'Which login a call runs as') still makes no gh call at all for an org bound to an isolated space that names no gh_config_dir: its docs are not synced, its PRs are dropped from the PR watcher and reviews are refused; docs/INSTALL.md still tells users to give each job its own account. SP-046 did not change this (outside its scope). Decide whether SP-063's rule changes under D-59 (and in which feature).

reconvene.topic: Per-space logins kept in the macOS keychain are outside the denied folders (security audit, unconfirmed high)
reconvene.detail: 2026-11-14 audit of PR #171: denying another space's gh_config_dir or claude_config_dir denies the folder, but gh's default keyring storage keeps the token in the login keychain (service gh:github.com, account = the GitHub login) and Claude Code on macOS keeps its login in the keychain too. If a sandboxed shell can reach the keychain, a session in one space could use another space's account (e.g. gh auth token --user <login>). Not measured: the probe would run a credential command, which agents here must not; the user can measure it (reporting only success or failure). Mitigations: log per-space gh profiles in with 'gh auth login --insecure-storage' so the token stays in the denied folder; orchd could warn when a profile reports keyring storage; Bash denies for 'gh auth token' and 'security find-generic-password' as defence in depth. Documented in docs/internals/install.md Limits.
reconvene.note: 2026-11-14: to be measured by SP-046.4.a4 (metadata only, D-61). 2026-11-14, measured by SP-046.4.a4 (TestClaudeE2E two-logins/keychain at 6baf911, account metadata only): GH_CONFIG_DIR pointed at another space's profile folder is denied ('operation not permitted') both ways, but a session of a space naming its own gh profile wrote its own profile folder naming the default account (no token) and 'GH_CONFIG_DIR=<it> gh auth status' in its sandboxed shell reported 'Logged in to github.com account willesq (keyring)'. So the keychain is reachable from every sandboxed shell, and any gh login stored there can be used by naming its account; the high is confirmed. Also measured: adding ~/Library/Keychains to a session's sandbox denyRead stopped gh reaching the keyring ('The token in default is invalid'), and would break every keyring login in that session. Options: (a) for spaces naming their own profile, require 'gh auth login --insecure-storage' and deny ~/Library/Keychains to them (the default-login spaces still reach every keyring login); (b) require --insecure-storage for every login, including the default, and deny ~/Library/Keychains everywhere (gh's own token then sits in hosts.yml, readable to that space's shell); (c) accept: with keychain-stored logins the GitHub account is not a boundary between spaces (as D-59 already accepts for the single-login case) and document it. Needs a decision.

reconvene.topic: Claude Code settings files with hooks are editable from space sessions (security audit medium, existing before D-59)
reconvene.detail: 2026-11-14 audit: neither the checkout settings nor the launcher's --settings deny the file tools ~/.claude/settings.json and settings.local.json (shared by every space's sessions that name no claude_config_dir) or a launch folder's .claude/settings*.json. A session whose Edit is approved could add a hook, and hooks run outside the sandbox in the next session of any space. The checkout path had this before D-59. Claude Code's own protection of its settings files was not measured. Denying them in every space would also block the user asking an agent to change their own settings; needs a decision.
reconvene.note: Accepted 2026-11-14 in D-61: the SP-042 guard is the protection. 2026-11-14: docs/internals/install.md Limits now say the SP-042 guard, which refuses writes to ~/.claude/settings* and .claude/settings*, is the protection (D-61).

reconvene.topic: claude_config_dir validation and leftover per-space profiles (security audit lows)
reconvene.detail: 2026-11-14 audit lows: (1) validation refuses only an exact (case-insensitive) duplicate claude_config_dir; it does not refuse one nested in another space's, one equal to or inside a gh_config_dir, an isolated root or orch's data folder, ~/.claude itself, or two spellings of one folder through a link. (2) Earlier builds of this branch made <data dir>/spaces/<space>/claude profiles (with a /login and transcripts, and a keychain item); nothing removes them, though they stay denied to other spaces. (3) The launcher's --settings JSON is visible to other local users in ps (paths only; documented).
reconvene.note: 2026-11-14: unchanged by D-61. Related: an allowRead that would hold another space's denied folder (by link or real path) or holds a pattern character is now left out (so a gh_config_dir inside the default gh folder leaves default-login spaces without gh in the sandbox, silently); validation still does not refuse a gh_config_dir or claude_config_dir nested in another's, inside the default gh folder, or holding pattern characters.

reconvene.topic: gh in the sandbox needs enableWeakerNetworkIsolation and allowedDomains (D-61)
reconvene.detail: Measured 2026-11-14 (Claude Code 2.1.309): with allowRead alone gh fails ('deny network-outbound api.github.com:443', then 'x509: OSStatus -26276'); it works with sandbox.network.allowedDomains [api.github.com, github.com] and sandbox.enableWeakerNetworkIsolation: true (or network.allowMachLookup ['com.apple.trustd.agent']). orch writes both for every placed space's sessions. Trade-offs: Claude Code calls the trustd lookup 'a potential data exfiltration vector'; its messages say a machine whose sandbox has such a setting serves no 'device tools' (not measured); allowedDomains lets every sandboxed program, not only gh and git (which the SP-044 outbound check reads), reach github.com without an approval. The security audit rated it medium. Options: keep; write them only for spaces that opt in to gh in the sandbox; use allowMachLookup instead of the boolean.

reconvene.topic: GitHub Enterprise and other gh hosts are not in allowedDomains
reconvene.detail: orch adds only api.github.com and github.com to sandbox.network.allowedDomains. A space whose gh profile logs in to a GitHub Enterprise host, or gh commands that reach other hosts (release downloads from objects.githubusercontent.com, codeload.github.com), still need an approval a headless session cannot give. orch never reads hosts.yml to learn the host.

reconvene.topic: Settings orch did not write can re-open its sandbox denies (security audit high, measured)
reconvene.detail: 2026-11-14 audit of PR #171, measured with Claude Code 2.1.309: with orch's denyRead of a folder in a checkout's settings.local.json, a sandboxed cat of a file in it succeeded when the checkout's own .claude/settings.json (a repository can commit one) or the same settings.local.json held sandbox.filesystem.allowRead of that folder (TestClaudeE2E 'loosening': job B's file read = true); a settings.json excludedCommands ['cat'] did not unsandbox cat; a session started as 'orch run' starts it (denies in --settings) was not re-opened by the same file (read = false). Under auto, an isolated space alone gets no rules, so its unsandboxed sessions could plant such entries before rules arrive (audit medium). orch now reports such entries, and settings files it cannot check, in each sync's problems and as 'orch run' warnings, but cannot remove them: a tracked settings.json is the repository's, and SP-046.1.a2 keeps users' own entries. Options: (a) require 'orch run' for isolated spaces' Claude Code sessions (its denies held); (b) have the guard (SP-041) refuse tool calls in a checkout whose settings re-open a deny; (c) take loosening entries out of settings.local.json (amending SP-046.1.a2) and handle settings.json with (a) or (b); (d) make 'orch run' refuse to launch from a folder whose settings loosen the rules unless --force (re-audit suggestion); (e) accept and document. Blocks SP-046 (DOD-6).

reconvene.topic: A forged sandbox setting is taken at restart and never marks a digest (security audit medium)
reconvene.detail: D-61 makes the setting quiet: it shows in orch status and the app, not in start digests. A process running as the user (not a sandboxed shell: orch.db is outside every space's writable folders, and the guard refuses tool calls naming it) can write a matching spaces_enforcement row and log entry for 'off' while orchd is stopped; the next start takes it with no problem, as it would a switch, but no digest says so. An inconsistent edit now makes the setting on and is reported. Options: (a) name the setting in the next digest once after each change or restart where it is off; (b) a keyed MAC over the row and log, with the key outside orch.db; (c) accept as D-61 decided. Blocks SP-046 (DOD-6) until decided.

reconvene.topic: auto judges only isolated roots, not other spaces' login folders (security audit medium)
reconvene.detail: D-61: auto writes rules 'only when another isolated space exists whose folders they would deny'. A policy with one isolated job and a personal or public space that names its own gh_config_dir (stored with --insecure-storage) or claude_config_dir gives the job's checkouts no rules, so nothing denies its sessions those folders or <data>/spaces/.orch (users' settings backups and the list of every space's checkouts). Options: (a) also write rules when the rules would deny another space's login folder; (b) always write them while .orch holds anything; (c) keep D-61's text and document it (done in docs/internals/install.md Limits). Blocks SP-046 (DOD-6) until decided.

reconvene.topic: Security audit lows and info on the D-61 rules
reconvene.detail: From the 2026-11-14 audits of PR #171: (1) deny paths are written as the policy spells them plus their real path, not their on-disk case; a root spelled in another case relies on the sandbox matching case-insensitively (not measured); (2) samePlace compares case-sensitively (safe: the default folder is then denied, not exposed); (3) spaces.SwitchHistory also returns sandbox-setting entries, whose Layer is not a layer (no caller today); (4) Loosening does not read ~/.claude settings, managed settings or other --settings files, does not expand '~user/', and cleans '..' before resolving links. Fixed in the same PR: link and real forms of an allowRead are dropped together, an allowRead with a pattern character is never written, a setting that does not verify or cannot be read is on, and settings files are read without following links, blocking or reading more than 4 MiB.

reconvene.topic: The orch installed on this Mac has no tool guard, so D-61's allowRead exposes the default gh folder by name until it is upgraded
reconvene.detail: 2026-11-14: the installed orch is 0.45.1 (commit cf031dc), whose Claude Code hooks have no PreToolUse entry. In the first TestClaudeE2E run of this branch, a session in a default-login space with orch's new allowRead of ~/.config/gh ran 'cat ~/.config/gh/config.yml | wc -c' and got the file's size: neither the installed hooks nor cc-safety-net refused it (the Read tool was refused by the installed Read(~/.config/gh/**) rule). The gh-guard probe now runs this tree's orch-hook and is refused (self_protection). Per-checkout files from this branch only reach the user when this release is installed with its PreToolUse hook; until then nothing changes. After upgrading, check 'orch status' lists the tool hooks and 'orch spaces enforce' shows the guard enforcing. With the guard off or logging, a default-login space's shell can read ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml (with keyring storage it names the account but holds no token).

reconvene.topic: Local files under a public root can be steered into public by any job session (security audit medium)
reconvene.detail: SP-030 makes a public root alone insufficient for checkouts without a verified-public GitHub remote (D-50), but anything local under a public root can still be written by any job session: the guard and the sandbox allow writes to public roots. Sessions may register repo/owner sources (SaveSource is refused to queued tasks only), and owner sources pick up new folders automatically. A session can therefore copy one job's files into a plain folder under ~/code, or into a folder whose fake .git names a public GitHub repo, or into the uncommitted working tree of a real public checkout, and the sources refresh places that content in public. This is not a regression (before SP-030 everything under a public root went to public), but the gate cannot meet 'only verified-public content reaches public' for local files. Options: (a) local files never go to public automatically: sources content under a public root goes to quarantine (or public_root_sessions); public content comes only from the GitHub docs sync, bound web prefixes and operator retags (SP-071). (b) Keep local placement in public and make repo/owner source registration operator-only (also RC-121/RC-122). This narrows the gap but does not close it, because owner sources still walk new folders and agents can still write into public checkouts. (c) Accept it and rely on the SP-046 sandbox denying job sessions writes to public roots. Recommendation: (a). Blocks SP-030 (DOD-6) until decided.

reconvene.topic: What counts as declaring a folder public (D-50)
reconvene.detail: Implemented as follows. A checkout under a public root is public only when GitHub reports its repo public, or when the operator bound a public root at the checkout's own folder or inside it. Content that is in no checkout (no .git anywhere above it, a symlinked .git included) is placed by the public root that holds it, following the summary's 'files under a root the operator declared public'. Confirm, or quarantine non-checkout content too (see RC-400).

reconvene.topic: Limits of leaving public on a visibility change
reconvene.detail: (1) When the repo listing fails, every repo keeps its docs as last indexed, public ones included. A listing failure is not treated as unreadable visibility for every repo, because that would delete and re-embed a whole public org after a network blip. (2) A repo missing from the listing (deleted, transferred out, or not visible to the account) keeps its public docs until the owner is purged. (3) Leaving public deletes and re-ingests (re-embeds); it is not a move. SP-024 must make DeleteSource remove a source from every collection. (4) Cost: each docs sync reads one stored copy per doc of every listed repo that is not verified public, and each repo/owner source refresh reads one per stored doc. (5) A repo lookup that GitHub was not asked about or did not answer (budget spent, cache only, rate limit, 5xx, network error) moves nothing until GitHub answers; only a not-found answer counts as private. Rewrites still quarantine unknown visibility. (6) These deletions bypass the prune guard by design, because capping them would keep non-public content readable everywhere. A not-found answer during a GitHub incident could still remove many public copies at once (security audit residual).

reconvene.topic: SP-030 security audit lows and design choices
reconvene.detail: (1) orchd's log names a repo or checkout path whose docs left public; tasks can read that log, but the content was public until then. (4) With an applied policy that no longer verifies, public copies are not moved; readers must treat a stale labels_v as unreadable (INV-08, SP-027). features.title: Measure Qdrant costs of a collection per space
features.summary: Benchmark search latency across several collections fused with RRF versus one filtered collection, and measure set_payload relabel throughput.
features.why: R-03 changes the storage layout; the cost must be measured, not assumed.

checkpoints.title: Baseline

acceptance.check: Hybrid search p50/p95 on one collection of 40,000 synthetic chunks with a payload filter, 200 queries.

evidence: a1: TestIntegrationSpacesCost (internal/rag/spaces_bench_it_test.go; ORCH_QDRANT_BENCH=1, qdrant v1.17.1 native, Apple M3 Max 16 cores, 2026-11-08). One hybrid collection of 40,000 synthetic chunks (384-d dense clustered around 256 centres, BM25 from the real tokenizer over a Zipf vocabulary), searched through Service.Search (hybrid, weighted ranking, TopK 10) with payload filter tags any [space:s0 space:s1] (50% of chunks), 200 queries after 20 warm-up. Default segments (auto): p50 16.45 ms, p95 17.06 ms. With ORCH_QDRANT_BENCH_SEGMENTS=2: p50 11.22 ms, p95 11.77 ms. Recorded.

checkpoints.title: Multi-collection

acceptance.check: Same corpus split across 4 collections; search the 2 allowed collections and fuse.
acceptance.threshold: <= 1.3x baseline, else document and revisit R-03

acceptance.check: Relabel by set_payload with a filter over 40,000 chunks.

evidence: a1: TestIntegrationSpacesCost, same corpus split across 4 collections; the 2 allowed collections searched in parallel through Service.Search (each with its own space tag filter as the second layer) and fused by RRF (k=60), 200 queries interleaved with the baseline. features.title: Verify how harness sandbox and permission settings layer
features.summary: Determine which settings files apply to a session started in a subfolder, whether per-space CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR profiles work (including whether they need a separate login), and what the Codex sandbox can deny.

checkpoints.title: Claude Code

acceptance.check: With a temp home: a sandbox denyRead on a folder blocks 'cat' into it; a Read(...) permission deny blocks the Read tool; record which of user, project and local settings apply when launched from a subfolder.

evidence: Recorded 2026-11-08, Claude Code 2.1.309, 16 headless `claude -p --model haiku` sessions in scratch git repos under the session scratchpad (user approved 11 + 5 runs on 2026-11-08). The user chose 'use my real config read-only' over logging in to a temp profile, so the user layer is the unmodified ~/.claude/settings.json; its env key DISABLE_TELEMETRY served as the user-layer marker. Every other layer set a distinct env marker read back with `env | grep`.

Layering matrix: L2 from checkout root -> user, project settings.json, local settings.local.json. L3 from repo/sub with its own .claude/ -> user, ROOT local, sub project, sub local; root project NOT applied. L4 from repo/sub/deep (no .claude) -> user, ROOT local only; root project NOT applied. L6 (fresh repo2/sub/deep) confirms L4: user + root local only. L5 from a non-git child of a dir with .claude/ -> user only.

Sandbox: S1 (root of sbx1; project sandbox.enabled=true, allowUnsandboxedCommands=false, filesystem.denyRead=[jobB]; local denyRead=[jobC]) -> `cat` of both fails 'Operation not permitted', so project and local denyRead merge and project enabled=true overrides user enabled=false. S1c same repo -> Read tool RETURNED jobB's file: sandbox denyRead does not block the Read tool. S1b2 (sbx1/sub, --permission-mode default) -> both files printed, consistent with root project settings not applying from a subfolder.

Read deny: S2 (project deny Read(//<abs jobC>/**), sandbox on) -> Read tool error 'File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings'. S2b2 same repo, Bash `cat` -> 'Operation not permitted': a Read deny also feeds the sandbox's denied reads. S2c from sbx2/sub -> file read (project settings not applied). S3 single-slash Read(/<abs>/**) -> not blocked (resolved relative to the settings file). S4/S4b (deny in ROOT settings.local.json) -> Read blocked from the root and from a subfolder.

Separate login: L0 fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and L1 temp HOME both exit 1 with 'Not logged in · Please run /login', so a per-space CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR profile needs its own login; persistence of that login per profile was not tested (the user declined the temp-profile login). S1b/S2b first runs were refused by the user's auto-mode classifier before reaching the sandbox (inconclusive), rerun as S1b2/S2b2 with --permission-mode default.
Matrix and conclusions recorded in docs/internals/install.md 'Harness sandbox and permission layering'.

features.title: Session liveness and session list
features.summary: orchd decides whether each pinned session is still running from the kernel, not from hook events: the pin's harness PID must exist with the same process start time. States: active (process alive, a hook event in the last 30 min), idle (process alive, no event for 30 min or more; a session left open for a week stays idle, not ended), ended (SessionEnd received, or the process is gone, or the PID now belongs to a different process; ended_at is the time orchd noticed), unpinned (a running claude, codex or gemini process with no pin, e.g. started before the hooks were installed). A sweep runs every 60 s. 'orch sessions list [--all]' and a ListSessions RPC show harness, session id, PID, space, pinned directory, state, last activity, tool-event count and refusals. A resumed session (SessionStart source=resume in a new process) rebinds the pin to the new PID and start time but never changes its space.
features.why: Sessions are often left open without /exit for days. Log retention and pins must follow the real process, not the last message.

A reused PID with a different start time marks the old session ended and never maps it to the new process.

features.title: Log retention sweeper
features.summary: orchd deletes a session's events N days after it ended (N = 3, 7 or 30; default 7), where 'ended' comes from SP-017: SessionEnd, or the process gone. A session whose process is still alive is never treated as ended, however long it has been idle; instead its log is capped at 50 MB, oldest non-refusal records first. Refusal records are kept 90 days. A total size cap (default 500 MB) deletes the oldest ended sessions first.
features.why: D-05. The log must not grow without bound.

checkpoints.title: Rules

A live session over 50 MB drops its oldest non-refusal records first; the total cap deletes the oldest ended sessions first and never touches a live session.
Sweeping twice changes nothing the second time; chain heads of deleted sessions are kept.

This is a documented exception to the hook never-block contract: while the guard is in an enforcing state, a timeout or unreadable input means refuse. features.title: Per-job GitHub account follow-ups
features.summary: Follow-ups to SP-063 decided on 2026-11-10 (D-54): scopes and PR watching for orgs reachable only through a space's profile; GitHub calls a space's profile cannot read are refused, with stricter gh_config_dir checks; the repo picker and PR-outcome tracker use the space's profile; a GitHub API quota cap per isolated account. acceptance.check: An org reachable only through a space's gh profile can be added to GitHub scopes and its PRs are watched and reviewed through that profile, never the default login.

A GitHub call made for a space through a profile that cannot read the target (repo or org outside the profile's access) is refused with a clear error, never retried with another login; gh_config_dir must be an absolute, owner-only directory under the user's home or the call is refused.
The repo picker and the PR-outcome tracker use the space's profile for that space's repos; a test shows the default login is not used for an isolated space's repo.
Each isolated account has a configurable GitHub API budget per hour; past it orchd defers that account's sync and watch calls (logged), while other accounts are unaffected.

With no space naming a gh profile, docs sync, PR watching, reviews, the guard's GitHub checks and generated checkout settings all use the default gh login, with no extra setup and no GH_CONFIG_DIR set; a space that names gh_config_dir uses that profile and never the default for its orgs.

orch detects, per space, which gh login and which Claude config it will use (default or the space's own) and whether each is authenticated, using only 'gh auth status'-style metadata; no token, cookie or credential file content is read, logged or stored.
'orch status' and the app's Spaces section show each space's login source (default or own profile) and its state; a test covers one-login and two-login layouts.
docs/INSTALL.md and OPERATIONS.md describe the single-login default, how to add a per-space gh profile or Claude config, and the trade-off that one login is not a boundary between jobs.

progress_file.purpose: Live progress for the user and the next session. The plan's status only changes on main when a PR merges; this file shows what is happening now. It is never committed (listed in .git/info/exclude).

schema.note: one plain sentence for the user: what is happening or what you need from them

status_values.superseded: retired by an explicit user decision; kept for history, never deleted

session_procedure: 1. Sync. In the main checkout (/Users/williamesquivel/code/willesq/orchestrator) run `git fetch origin`. Read the plan from origin/main: `git show origin/main:docs/spaces/spaces-features.json`. That copy is authoritative for status; local copies may be stale.

2. Pick exactly one feature: the first feature in ascending 'priority' whose status on origin/main is not 'done' or 'superseded'. Never skip it, never choose another, never work on two at once. Run one session at a time.

3. Look for existing work on it. First read the live progress file (/Users/williamesquivel/code/willesq/orchestrator/docs/spaces/progress.local.json): if it names a different session_id with status 'in_progress' and updated_at less than 30 minutes ago, another session is working. Stop and tell the user. Then check branches and PRs: the branch is feat/<id in lowercase>-<short-slug> (e.g. feat/sp-020-spaces-config); run `git branch -a --list '*feat/<id>-*'` and `gh pr list --state all --search '<ID> in:title'`.

3a. If an open PR exists whose plan copy already shows the feature 'done' with verification, it is waiting for the user to review and merge. Report the PR link and stop. Do not start the next feature.

3b. If a branch or open PR exists but the feature isn't done there, resume it: use its existing worktree under /Users/williamesquivel/code/willesq/orchestrator.worktrees/feat/..., or recreate it with ~/.claude/orchestrator/scripts/git_worktree_create.sh <branch> and answer 'y' to reuse the existing branch.
3c. If the PR was merged but origin/main doesn't show the feature done, or a PR was closed unmerged, stop and ask the user what happened.
3d. If nothing exists, run ~/.claude/orchestrator/scripts/git_worktree_create.sh feat/<id>-<slug> from the main checkout and work only in that worktree.

4. Preconditions. Every depends_on feature must be 'done' on origin/main, and no entry in decisions.open may list this feature in 'blocks'. If either fails, stop and tell the user. (Priority order makes the first case unexpected.)

5. On the feature branch, set the feature's status to 'in_progress', increment 'attempts', and set 'branch'. Commit (signed). Push, open a draft PR titled 'feat(spaces): <summary> (<ID>)' early, record its URL in the feature's 'pr' field, and register it in ~/.pr-watch.json. Write the live progress file now and after every later step, checkpoint, block or finish (schema in plan_location.progress_file); make sure docs/spaces/progress.local.json is listed in the main checkout's .git/info/exclude.

6. Do the checkpoints in order. After each one, record evidence (test names, command output, measured numbers, or 'confirmed by user on <date>' for manual items) in that checkpoint's 'evidence' array and commit. Update the live progress file (checkpoint, checkpoints_done, note, a history entry) at the start and end of each checkpoint.

7. Manual items need the user: ask them to perform or confirm the step and wait. If you can't continue for any reason (missing input, a criterion that is wrong or impossible, 3 failed fix rounds), set status 'blocked' with a specific blocked_reason, commit, push, and stop. Never move past a blocked feature. When you stop or need the user, the live file's status and note must say so.

8. When every checkpoint has evidence meeting its threshold, run every definition_of_done check yourself. Then spawn an independent verifier: a fresh subagent that gets only the diff (origin/main...HEAD), this feature's JSON, the invariants it appears in, and definition_of_done. It re-runs every test, command and metric itself and reports pass or fail for each acceptance item and each DOD check. It does not see your reasoning.

9. If the verifier reports any failure, fix it and verify again, up to 3 rounds; after that, set 'blocked'. If everything passes, set status 'done', passes=true, verified_sha to the commit that was verified, verified_at to the current UTC time (ISO 8601). Commit that change (signed) and push. Leave the PR as a draft; the user marks it ready and merges.

10. Never delete, renumber or reorder features, checkpoints or acceptance items, and never edit acceptance criteria (criteria_sha256 detects it). Only the user may mark a feature 'superseded'. If you discover new work, describe it under 'Proposed new features' in the PR body; it is appended to the plan, with the next free ID, only after the user approves.

11. Finish with a short report: the feature, its PR link, the verification result, what is waiting on the user, and which feature step 2 will pick next once this one is merged. Leave the live progress file with the final status ('done', 'blocked' or 'idle') and a note matching your report.

12. Record decisions as you go, until the last feature is done. A decision the user makes goes to decisions.confirmed_by_user with the next D-id and the date. Everything else that needs the user later goes to decisions.reconvene with the next RC-id: proposed features or acceptance items (also listed in the PR body per step 10), low or accepted security findings, deferred follow-ups, unverified assumptions, and actions the user must take. Give each a kind (decision, follow-up or user-action), topic, detail, source (PR, issue or session URI), raised date, affects and status 'open'. Reconvene items never block work; an item the user settles moves to confirmed_by_user (or becomes a feature) and its status becomes 'resolved' with a note. Before reporting in step 11, check that your session's items are recorded.
